global_parameter.name: bank color
global_parameter.tooltip: color of the preset

global_parameter.name: led attenuation
global_parameter.tooltip: attenuation of the brightness of the led

global_parameter.name: usb audio
global_parameter.tooltip: what the minichord does with the sound of the phone or computer it is plugged into. 0: as it always has, it is offered as a speaker and what is sent to it is not played (a phone sends all its sound there, and goes quiet). 1: it is played through the minichord, beside the instrument, for playing along. 2: it is not offered as a speaker, so the phone or computer keeps its own sound. In every case the minichord's own sound can be recorded over USB. A setting of the instrument, not of a preset: it stays as chosen whichever preset is loaded. Changing to or from 2 restarts the minichord a moment later, since the phone or computer only learns what it offers when it connects

global_parameter.name: harp plate
global_parameter.tooltip: which harp plate is fitted, for the plates that are read between their zones. 0 is the stock strip, and any plate with twelve separate zones. 1 is zipper 24: a finger on the band between two zones touches both and plays the note between them, for 24 strings, the top one the band where the top zone meets an island of the bottom zone: two octaves of 12-EDO, or one of 24-EDO. The extra strings play in chromatic mode and the scale modes, which carry on up the scale; chord mode still plays twelve. 2 is the arcade wheel: its zones play as they are, and while a finger is on the ring it sends where, as control change 23 on the harp channel (0 at the top, counting clockwise to 127), with control change 24 at 127 as the finger lands and 0 as it leaves. 3 is the fretless wrap: twelve zones that taper into one another, with an island of the bottom zone above the top one; it plays as the stock strip does, and with harp ribbon the island is a thirteenth place, a whole octave in chromatic mode (zipper 24 wraps the ribbon the same way). Set it to 0 for any other plate: at 1 every other note goes missing, and at 3 a finger at the top with another on the bottom pad can read as the island

global_parameter.name: harp touch threshold
global_parameter.tooltip: how firm a touch the harp needs before a zone counts as touched; higher needs a firmer finger. 0 is the stock 40. A plate with smaller zones reads weaker and may want less. Takes effect once no zone is touched

global_parameter.name: harp release threshold
global_parameter.tooltip: how far a finger rises before a touched zone lets go: the zone lets go when its reading falls under this. Higher lets go sooner, lower holds on longer. 0 is the stock 20, and it is kept under the touch threshold. On the string plates it sets where on the way up pluck on lift sounds. Takes effect once no zone is touched

global_parameter.name: chord key signature
global_parameter.tooltip: automatically makes flat or sharp the chords for a particular key. 0=C, 1=G, 2=D, 3=A, 4=E, 5=B, 6=F, 7=Bb, 8=Eb, 9=Ab, 10=Db, 11=Gb, and the enharmonic keys 12=F#, 13=C#, 14=G#, 15=D#, 16=A#, 17=E#, 18=B#, 19=Fb, 20=Cb

global_parameter.name: sharp function
global_parameter.tooltip: change the sharp button to a flat button

global_parameter.name: transpose
global_parameter.tooltip: transpose all sounds by a number of semitones

global_parameter.name: temperament
global_parameter.tooltip: tuning of the notes: 0=equal, 1=quarter-comma meantone, 2=five-limit just (C major), 3=pythagorean, 4=werckmeister III, 5=kirnberger III, 6=vallotti, 7=young no. 2, 8=kellner, 9=sixth-comma meantone, 10=19-EDO, 11=24-EDO (quarter tones), 12=31-EDO, 13=your own (own temperament C to B, which a Scala file or a MIDI Tuning Standard message from a computer also sets). A keeps the master tuning pitch in the twelve-note ones, which are fixed to the keyboard, sweetest around C, so far keys sound progressively rougher, as they did historically. 10 and 11 divide the octave differently instead

global_parameter.name: modifier step
global_parameter.tooltip: how far the modifier moves a note, in the divided octaves. 0 as the tuning has it: the chromatic semitone in 19 and 31, a quarter-tone in 24. 1 one step of the tuning: the diesis of 31 (C to C half-sharp, 39 cents), the quarter-tone of 24, the semitone of 19. 2 the chromatic semitone in every one, so 24 plays the semitones again. Key signatures still sharpen and flatten by the semitone. In twelve it changes nothing

global_parameter.name: purity
global_parameter.tooltip: draws every note from its tempered pitch toward the just interval it makes with the root of the chord being played, in percent: thirds toward 5/4 and 6/5, fifths toward 3/2, a dominant seventh's seventh toward 7/4, the neutral third of 31 toward 11/9, and the harp's notes toward the same root, so they sit in the chord. Put it on a knob or hover and a held chord goes from beating to still under the hand. The chord's root stays where the temperament puts it, so the tuning never drifts from chord to chord. Steps with no simple ratio near them keep their pitch. In MPE the pure pitch goes out as each voice's bend. 0 tempered, as before

global_parameter.name: drone
global_parameter.tooltip: a drone on the key's Sa under everything, to hear every interval against, as a raga or a maqam is learnt and played: 1 a tanpura, its four strings plucked in turn over and over, Pa below Sa, Sa, Sa, and Sa an octave down, each buzzing on its bridge as it rings; 2 the same with Ma in place of Pa (for ragas without Pa); 3 with Ni (for ragas like Marwa); 4 all Sa; 5 a shruti box, Sa, Pa and the Sa below as reeds, breathing slowly. Sa is the key, the chord key signature's root (where the harp's scales start) and the transpose, at the temperament's pitch, and the strings around it are tuned pure. It plays whether or not rhythm mode is on; put it under the double tap to bring it in and out. 0 off

global_parameter.name: drone level
global_parameter.tooltip: how loud the drone is, in percent; at 50 it sits under the harp

global_parameter.name: drone pace
global_parameter.tooltip: how long the tanpura player waits from one string to the next, in tenths of a second, with one more wait before each round: 12, the usual, plucks a round every six seconds. Not for the shruti box

global_parameter.name: drone register
global_parameter.tooltip: where the drone's Sa sits: 0 low, from E2 to E3 (a male singer's tanpura), 1 middle, from A2 to A3, 2 high, from D3 to D4 (a female singer's). The lowest string is an octave below

global_parameter.name: drone reverb
global_parameter.tooltip: how much of the drone goes into the reverb, in percent, so a tanpura sits in the same room as a reverberant santoor or harp; it stays as loud dry. 0 dry, as before

global_parameter.name: own temperament C
global_parameter.tooltip: temperament 13's C: how far it sits from equal temperament, in tenths of a cent from 1000, so 1000 is equal, 863 is 13.7 cents flat and 1140 14 cents sharp (-100 to +100 cents). The twelve make your own temperament, as a Scala file of twelve notes does; the editor can read one in, and a MIDI Tuning Standard scale/octave or bulk dump message from a computer sets all twelve and selects it. A at 1000 keeps A on the master tuning pitch

global_parameter.name: master tuning
global_parameter.tooltip: reference pitch for A4, in tenths of a Hz: 4400 = 440.0 Hz, 4420 = 442.0 Hz. Range 432.0-446.0 Hz. Retunes the synth only; MIDI note numbers are unchanged
global_parameter.method: { int tenths = (value == 0) ? 4400 : constrain(value, 4320, 4460); float tuned_c_frequency = 130.81 * (tenths / 4400.0); if (tuned_c_frequency != c_frequency) { c_frequency = tuned_c_frequency; retune_active_voices(); } }

global_parameter.name: chord channel
global_parameter.tooltip: set the midi channel for the chord section

global_parameter.name: harp channel
global_parameter.tooltip: set the midi channel for the harp section

global_parameter.name: single port mode
global_parameter.tooltip: puts both the chord and the harp on the same midi port

global_parameter.name: MPE output
global_parameter.tooltip: gives every voice its own midi channel (MPE), so glide and the real pitch of a temperament or a divided octave survive the trip out; off is the usual single channel output

global_parameter.name: MTS output
global_parameter.tooltip: outside MPE, retunes each note's key just before it starts with a MIDI Tuning Standard message (single note tuning change, real time), so a synth that reads MTS (Surge, Pianoteq, Vital, many hardware synths) plays the divided octaves, the temperaments, purity, a string's bend and the master tuning as the minichord sounds them, on one channel. Two notes that leave as one key share its tuning: in 31, C# and Db are the same key. MPE output, when on, carries the pitch instead. 0 off, as before

global_parameter.name: harp note-off on lift
global_parameter.tooltip: when a harp string's midi note ends. At 0 it lasts as long as the string sounds, through the release, so a strum arrives as ringing strings; a palm mute ends them all at once. At 1 it ends as the finger lifts, as before, leaving the release to whatever is receiving. With harp pluck on lift, at 1 it ends as the string starts to fade

global_parameter.name: MIDI in plays
global_parameter.tooltip: plays notes sent to the minichord over USB, as a sound module: on the harp's port and channel the harp strings (twelve voices), on the chords' port and channel the chord voices (four), the ones it sends its own notes on, by default the chords on port 1 and the harp on port 2, both on channel 1. Notes sound at their true pitch, whatever the preset's octaves and transpose, in the minichord's tuning and temperament; velocity sets their loudness, and a string's brightness; the sustain pedal holds them. Playing the minichord itself takes a voice back. Off, as a computer that echoes the minichord's own notes back to it would double them

global_parameter.name: knobs send MIDI
global_parameter.tooltip: sends the three knobs' positions out over MIDI as they turn, as control changes 20 (chord knob), 21 (harp knob) and 22 (modulation knob) on the chord channel, so they can be MIDI-learnt in a DAW or read by a program; the knobs keep doing their usual jobs

global_parameter.name: reverb size
global_parameter.tooltip: size of the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb high damping
global_parameter.tooltip: damping of high frequencies in the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb low damping
global_parameter.tooltip: damping of low frequencies in the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb low pass
global_parameter.tooltip: additional low pass in the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb diffusion
global_parameter.tooltip: diffusion within the reverb room

global_parameter.name: speed ramp
global_parameter.tooltip: how long the tremolo and the vibrato, harp and chords, take to reach a new rate, in tenths of a second, instead of jumping to it: as a rotating speaker's rotors spin up when switched to fast and coast down when switched to slow, taking half again as long to slow. Put the chords' tremolo or vibrato frequency under the double tap or a knob and the organ's speaker winds up and down: about 10 for its horn, 40 for its drum. Loading a preset sets the rates at once. 0 jumps, as before

global_parameter.name: string spread
global_parameter.tooltip: fans the harp strings out across the stereo field, in percent of the full width: 0 keeps them all in the middle, as before. Centred on where pan puts the harp. How they are laid out is spread pattern

global_parameter.name: spread pattern
global_parameter.tooltip: how string spread lays the strings out. 0: by pitch, the lowest string to the left and the highest to the right, like sitting at a harp; ribbon and incoming notes land by their pitch too. 1: neighbouring strings on alternate sides, so a strum ping-pongs

global_parameter.name: chord ensemble
global_parameter.tooltip: a slow stereo chorus on the chords, the classic ensemble sound: a slightly swept copy on each side, moving at different rates, widens them and gives them a gentle shimmer. 0 is off, as before; 100 is half dry and half chorus

global_parameter.name: vocoder
global_parameter.tooltip: the chords (or the harp, see vocoder carrier) take on the shape of the sound coming in over USB, so they talk or sing with it: speech, singing or drums from the phone or computer. In percent of the vocoded sound in place of the dry; 0 is off, as before. The minichord has no microphone, so the voice has to come over USB, which needs usb audio 0 or 1 (0: only the vocoded chords are heard; 1: the incoming sound is heard too). With nothing coming in, the vocoded part is silent

global_parameter.name: vocoder carrier
global_parameter.tooltip: what the vocoder shapes. 0: the chords, the classic sustained vocoder sound. 1: the harp, whose plucks die away too fast to carry words well but make textures. 2: both, the harp's vocoded part coming through the chords' effects

global_parameter.name: vocoder consonants
global_parameter.tooltip: how much of the incoming sound's hiss (s, t, sh) the vocoder lets through, so words can be made out. 0 is a pure vocoder, only the chords' own sound

global_parameter.name: phone follow 1 control
global_parameter.tooltip: which setting the music coming in over USB moves, the way hover does: from as the preset has it with the music quiet to phone follow 1 value at its loudest. Works on whatever plays into the minichord, from a phone or a computer, heard through the minichord or not (USB audio 0 or 1, not 2). Loud is the music's own: it is measured against the loudest it has been in the last few seconds, so the phone's volume doesn't matter. Chord volume with value 0 and the bass band ducks the chords under every kick; the chord filter's cutoff with a high value and the treble band opens it on every hat. Any setting a knob can take. With knobs send MIDI on it also goes out as control change 26 on the chord channel. 0 leaves it unassigned

global_parameter.name: phone follow 1 value
global_parameter.tooltip: the value phone follow 1 control's setting reaches with the music at its loudest. Above or below the preset's own value, so the music can open a filter or close it, swell a sound or duck it

global_parameter.name: phone follow 1 band
global_parameter.tooltip: what phone follow 1 listens to: 0 the whole sound, 1 the bass under 150 Hz (the kick drum and bass line), 2 the treble over 6 kHz (hats, cymbals and the hiss of consonants)

global_parameter.name: phone follow 1 release
global_parameter.tooltip: how slowly phone follow 1 falls back as the music drops, in milliseconds; it rises as fast as the music does. Short (20-50) follows each hit, for a filter that opens on every hat; a few hundred lets ducked chords swell back between kicks, the pumping of sidechain compression; longer follows the music's swells rather than its beats

global_parameter.name: phone follow 2 control
global_parameter.tooltip: which setting the music coming in over USB moves, the way hover does: from as the preset has it with the music quiet to phone follow 2 value at its loudest. Works on whatever plays into the minichord, from a phone or a computer, heard through the minichord or not (USB audio 0 or 1, not 2). Loud is the music's own: it is measured against the loudest it has been in the last few seconds, so the phone's volume doesn't matter. Chord volume with value 0 and the bass band ducks the chords under every kick; the chord filter's cutoff with a high value and the treble band opens it on every hat. Any setting a knob can take. With knobs send MIDI on it also goes out as control change 27 on the chord channel. 0 leaves it unassigned

global_parameter.name: phone follow 2 value
global_parameter.tooltip: the value phone follow 2 control's setting reaches with the music at its loudest. Above or below the preset's own value, so the music can open a filter or close it, swell a sound or duck it

global_parameter.name: phone follow 2 band
global_parameter.tooltip: what phone follow 2 listens to: 0 the whole sound, 1 the bass under 150 Hz (the kick drum and bass line), 2 the treble over 6 kHz (hats, cymbals and the hiss of consonants)

global_parameter.name: phone follow 2 release
global_parameter.tooltip: how slowly phone follow 2 falls back as the music drops, in milliseconds; it rises as fast as the music does. Short (20-50) follows each hit, for a filter that opens on every hat; a few hundred lets ducked chords swell back between kicks, the pumping of sidechain compression; longer follows the music's swells rather than its beats

global_parameter.name: phone beat
global_parameter.tooltip: in rhythm mode, the rhythm follows the beat of the music coming in over USB: it finds the tempo (70 to 180 bpm) and, where a song could be heard at half or twice it, takes the one nearer the rhythm's own tempo, so set the tempo near the song's (or tap it once) to choose and is drawn onto the music's beats, as tap tempo draws it onto taps, and keeps following as the music speeds up or slows down. It takes a few seconds of steady beat to lock on, and lets go where there's no beat to find. It finds the beat, not the bar, so the pattern may start its bar on any beat. MIDI clock out and the looper in time follow along; a MIDI clock coming in has the rhythm instead. 0 off

global_parameter.name: phone kick stab
global_parameter.tooltip: each kick drum in the music coming in over USB strikes the chord held again, so the chord hand plays in the music's groove: hold a chord, or keep one with hold, and it sounds on every kick. Not in rhythm mode, which keeps its own time. 0 off

global_parameter.name: phone kick note
global_parameter.tooltip: each kick drum in the music coming in over USB sends this MIDI note on the chord channel, louder for a harder kick, so a drum machine or a computer can play along with the phone through the minichord. 36 is General MIDI's bass drum. 0 sends nothing

global_parameter.name: phone filter
global_parameter.tooltip: the DJ filter on the song coming in over USB, as it plays through the minichord (USB audio 1): below 100 a low pass, closing to 200 Hz at 0; above 100 a high pass, opening to 4 kHz at 200; 100 leaves the song as it is. A knob or hover swept across it sweeps the song from muffled to thin

global_parameter.name: phone filter resonance
global_parameter.tooltip: how much the DJ filter rings at its corner: 0 smooth, 100 a whistle

global_parameter.name: phone echo
global_parameter.tooltip: how much of the song goes into an echo in time with the music: the double tap (or tap and hold) set to 100 throws the song into it, and the echoes carry on as it closes, a dub throw. 0 sends nothing

global_parameter.name: phone echo time
global_parameter.tooltip: the echo's time, as a division of the beat: of the music's tempo where phone beat or phone strum has found it, of the rhythm's otherwise. 0 an eighth, 1 a dotted eighth, 2 a quarter, 3 a sixteenth, 4 an eighth triplet; at most 500 ms

global_parameter.name: phone echo feedback
global_parameter.tooltip: how much of each echo comes round again: 0 one echo, 90 a long trail

global_parameter.name: phone deck
global_parameter.tooltip: writing it does one thing and it goes back to 0, never kept: 1 the tape stop, the song slowing to a stop over 0.8 s as a turntable does when its power goes, and the next time the song back in; 2 grabs the last second of the song onto the harp, as voice source 5, as loud as it goes. Assign the double tap to it (double tap control 332) with value 1 or 2

global_parameter.name: phone strum
global_parameter.tooltip: the harp strums the chord held on the beat of the music coming in over USB, six strings in the middle, low to high: 1 on every beat, 2 down on the beat and up between, in eighths. It finds the beat as phone beat does, a few seconds of it; a chord must be held (or kept with hold). It rests on the ribbon, the zipper plate and with harp drums. 0 off

global_parameter.name: MIDI clock out
global_parameter.tooltip: sends rhythm mode's tempo out as MIDI clock (24 a beat), so a drum machine, a looper pedal or a computer plays in time with the minichord. 0 off, 1 on port 1 (the chords' by default), 2 on port 2 (the harp's), 3 on both. Only in rhythm mode: Start as it comes on (on the first beat of a bar), Stop as it goes off. Tap tempo and the default bpm move it. Nothing goes out while a MIDI clock is coming in: the minichord follows that one instead

global_parameter.name: looper quantize
global_parameter.tooltip: moves each looped note to the nearest point of a grid, so the loop plays back in time: 0 off, as played; 1 quarter notes; 2 eighths (the off one where shuffle value puts it); 3 sixteenths; 4 eighth triplets. The first pass plays as played and the loop is corrected as it closes; an overdub's notes as they come. Each note keeps its length. The grid is the looper's beat: rhythm mode's, or its own at the default bpm from where the loop starts

global_parameter.name: looper count-in
global_parameter.tooltip: bars counted in before a recording starts: 0 none, it starts at once as before; 1 or 2 bars. The recording starts on the bar line after them (in rhythm mode, the first bar line at least that far off); a note played just before it, reaching for the downbeat, starts the loop. The LED flashes red on the beats. Pair it with looper click to hear them

global_parameter.name: looper click
global_parameter.tooltip: a metronome tick on the beats, higher on the first of a bar: 0 off; 1 through the count-in; 2 the count-in and the recording; 3 those and the loop playing. On the speaker and headphones only: the USB recording never has it. Its tempo is rhythm mode's, or the default bpm (control change 103 taps it too)

global_parameter.name: looper click level
global_parameter.tooltip: how loud the looper's click is

global_parameter.name: looper length
global_parameter.tooltip: how long a loop is, in bars: 0 as long as you play it, closed by the next step; 1 to 16 bars, and the recording closes by itself on that bar line and plays on without a gap, so a press to record is all it takes. A step before then closes it on the nearest bar line, recording on till it. Its bars are the rhythm style's, at rhythm mode's tempo, or the default bpm from where the loop starts. Pair it with looper count-in and looper click to hear where the bars fall

global_parameter.name: chord memory
global_parameter.tooltip: the chord memory, as on an Omnichord: a progression recorded in time with rhythm mode, then played back by itself, the accompaniment and the harp following it, so both hands are free for the strings. Writing it does one thing and it goes back to 0, never kept in a preset: 1 record, 2 play, 3 stop, 4 clear, 5 the next step. Control changes 104-108 do the same on any channel. Assign the double tap to it (double tap control 287) and each double tap takes the next step: record, play, stop, then record anew. It turns rhythm mode on. Recording starts on a bar line and each chord goes in on the nearest beat; it closes on the nearest bar line and plays on from there. A chord pressed while it plays stands until its next. The LED is violet, pulsing while it records

global_parameter.name: pan
global_parameter.tooltip: pans the chord and harp sound, from fully separated to both in the middle

global_parameter.name: double tap control
global_parameter.tooltip: which setting two quick taps of the modifier button toggle, with the settings of double tap control 2 and 3 if assigned. 0 leaves this pair unassigned. Set it to 39 to switch chord layouts, or to any other setting you want under a tap. Set it to 256 for the looper: each double tap then takes its next step, record, play, stop, and record a new loop, instead of toggling; with double tap value 7, the step goes to a looper on the computer (the Lab's looper page) instead of the minichord's own (best given the double tap on its own, since every assigned pair moves on each double tap)

global_parameter.name: double tap value
global_parameter.tooltip: the value the double tap applies. Tapping again puts back whatever was there before

global_parameter.name: double tap hold
global_parameter.tooltip: tap the modifier, then press it again and hold: the double tap's settings flip while it is held and flip back as it lets go, a momentary version of the double tap, for a filter thrown open or a sound muted for as long as the finger stays down. Let go as quickly as a tap and it latches, as a double tap does; a double tap already latched is let go while held, and comes back. The second press acts as it lands rather than as it lifts, and only with no chord held. While held so, the modifier doesn't sharpen a chord pressed meanwhile or switch the knobs to their alternates. The looper, chord memory and rhythm fill take their step as the press lands. 0: a held second press does nothing, as before

global_parameter.name: modifier with up and down
global_parameter.tooltip: holding the modifier, the preset buttons do two things for a performance going wrong: down reverts, putting the preset back as it was saved and dropping whatever the knobs, an editor or the double tap changed since it loaded (nothing is left to save); up is the panic, every voice stopped at once, the looper and chord memory stopped (keeping what they hold), and All Notes Off sent on every channel of both MIDI ports, while rhythm mode and hold stay as they are. Neither changes the preset. 0: the modifier makes no difference to up and down, as before

global_parameter.name: revert or panic
global_parameter.tooltip: writing it does one thing and it goes back to 0, never kept in a preset: 1 reverts the preset to as it was saved, 2 is the panic (see modifier with up and down). Assign the double tap to it (double tap control 323) for a revert each double tap, or the panic with double tap value 2

global_parameter.name: double tap control 2

harp_parameter.name: global gain
harp_parameter.tooltip: global gain of the harp section

harp_parameter.name: scalar harp mode
harp_parameter.tooltip: what the harp strings play. 0=follows the chord (default), 1=Major, 2=Major Pentatonic, 3=Minor Pentatonic, 4=Diminished 6th, 5=Relative Natural Minor, 6=Relative Harmonic Minor, 7=Relative Minor Pentatonic, 8=scale chosen per chord, 9=as 8 but pentatonic, 10=your own scale rooted on the key, 11=your own scale rooted on the chord, 12=the generator scale rooted on the key, 13=the generator scale rooted on the chord, 14=a maqam (see maqam) rooted on the key, 15=a maqam rooted on the chord

harp_parameter.name: custom scale
harp_parameter.tooltip: the scale used by scalar harp modes 10 and 11: tick the degrees you want. In 19, 24 and 31 each degree is read by its name, so b3 is that division's minor third and the scale keeps its sound; for steps twelve has no name for, tick them in the step scale, which plays in its place when any of its steps is ticked

harp_parameter.name: generator
harp_parameter.tooltip: the interval the generator scale (scalar harp modes 12 and 13) is built from, in steps of the tuning: the scale is this interval stacked again and again and folded into one octave, which is how a regular temperament makes its scales. In 31: 7 with 9 notes is Orwell[9], 18 with 7 the meantone diatonic, 9 with 7 Mohajira (neutral), 10 with 7 Magic, 3 with 10 Miracle. In 12: 7 is the fifth, with 5 notes the pentatonic and 7 the major scale. Counted in steps of whatever tuning is chosen, so the same numbers make a different scale in another; past the top of the octave it wraps round

harp_parameter.name: generator notes
harp_parameter.tooltip: how many notes the generator scale has: how many times the generator is stacked. A chain that comes back to the root before it is done (4 in 12 closes after three notes) keeps the notes it has

harp_parameter.name: generator mode
harp_parameter.tooltip: which rotation of the generator scale the harp plays: how many of its generators lie below the root. 0 builds the chain straight up from the root; each step up moves one generator under it. With 18 in 31 or 7 in 12 and 7 notes, 0 is Lydian, 1 major, 2 Mixolydian, 3 Dorian, 4 minor, 5 Phrygian, 6 Locrian. Past the number of notes it stays at the last

harp_parameter.name: step scale 0-10
harp_parameter.tooltip: the scale scalar harp modes 10 and 11 play in 19, 24 and 31, ticked step by step of the division rather than by name, for the notes twelve has no name for: the quarter-tones of 24, the dieses of 31 (C to C# is 2 of 31 and C to Db 3). Step 0 is the root and the steps count up the octave; this row is steps 0 to 10, the next two carry on to 30. With no step ticked the custom scale plays, its degrees read by name in the division. In twelve the custom scale always plays. Steps past the division's size are left out, so in 19 only 0 to 18 count

harp_parameter.name: step scale 11-21
harp_parameter.tooltip: steps 11 to 21 of the step scale (see step scale 0-10)

harp_parameter.name: step scale 22-30
harp_parameter.tooltip: steps 22 to 30 of the step scale, which only 24 (to 23) and 31 reach (see step scale 0-10)

harp_parameter.name: chromatic mode
harp_parameter.tooltip: puts the harp in chromatic mode, with static notes not dependant on chord selection

harp_parameter.name: harp rank
harp_parameter.tooltip: which twelve steps the chromatic harp plays, like the rows of strings on a triple harp: 1 is steps 1 to 12 of the division, 2 is 13 to 24, 3 is 25 to 36, carrying on past the octave where the division ends. 31 has three ranks, 19 and 24 have two, and in 12 there is only one, so this changes nothing there. Only in chromatic mode

harp_parameter.name: harp ribbon
harp_parameter.tooltip: play the harp as a ribbon controller: one fretless string along the strip, the pitch following the finger as it slides, gliding from each string's note to the next. Each finger sounds a voice of its own, and it sounds on touch whatever pluck on lift says. On the fretless plate, whose zones taper into one another, the pitch moves evenly along the strip; on the stock strip a finger mostly reads one zone, so the pitch rests on each note and slides where the finger bridges two (turn up ribbon glide to smooth the steps into a slide). In MPE the glide goes out as each voice's pitch bend; outside MPE the midi note follows the nearest string. A patch with some sustain holds a note under a still finger. Not on the arcade wheel

harp_parameter.name: ribbon span
harp_parameter.tooltip: how many strings the ribbon covers from the bottom of the strip to the top: fewer spreads each note wider and makes it easier to play in tune, more fits more range. 0 is the twelve strings of the plate, thirteen on the fretless wrap plate and zipper 24. In chromatic mode 13 is an octave and 25 would be two; in the scale modes the strings carry on up the scale. Chord mode has only its twelve

harp_parameter.name: ribbon snap
harp_parameter.tooltip: how strongly the ribbon holds to the strings' notes: this much of each string's width, in percent, plays its note in tune, and between the notes the pitch slides the rest of the way. 0 is fretless, 100 steps from note to note

harp_parameter.name: ribbon step snap
harp_parameter.tooltip: a second, lighter ribbon snap, for the notes between the strings: where two strings are more than one step of the tuning apart, the slide between them is held on each step it passes, this much of each step's width in percent. With ribbon snap high and this lower, the strings' notes are easy to find and the steps between them, a 31's dieses or a 24's quarter-tones, can still be landed on. 0 slides evenly between strings, as before

harp_parameter.name: melodic direction
harp_parameter.tooltip: a scale that goes down by other notes than it goes up, as a raga's aroha and avaroha, a maqam or melodic minor do: with this on, in scalar harp modes 10, 11, 14 and 15 each string plucked lower than the one before (a strum down, a falling line) plays the scale's down form, and each plucked higher the up form; a string plucked again keeps the direction it had. On the ribbon the slide says, once it has turned back a quarter of a string. Strings already ringing keep their pitch. The custom scale's down form is custom scale down, or step scale down in 19, 24 and 31; a maqam has its own. 0 the scale is the same both ways, as before

harp_parameter.name: custom scale down
harp_parameter.tooltip: the custom scale's down form, for melodic direction: the degrees the harp plays while the melody falls, read by name in 19, 24 and 31 as the custom scale is. Raga Khamaj, say: up 1 3 4 5 6 7, down 1 2 3 4 5 6 b7. With none ticked the scale goes down as it went up

harp_parameter.name: step scale down 0-10
harp_parameter.tooltip: the step scale's down form, for melodic direction in 19, 24 and 31: steps 0 to 10 of the division, the next two carrying on to 30. With any ticked it serves in place of custom scale down

harp_parameter.name: step scale down 11-21
harp_parameter.tooltip: steps 11 to 21 of the step scale's down form (see step scale down 0-10)

harp_parameter.name: step scale down 22-30
harp_parameter.tooltip: steps 22 to 30 of the step scale's down form, which only 24 and 31 reach (see step scale down 0-10)

harp_parameter.name: maqam
harp_parameter.tooltip: the maqam scalar harp modes 14 and 15 play, from the key or the chord's root: 0 Rast (C D E half-flat F G A B half-flat, coming down B flat), 1 Bayati (D E half-flat F G A Bb C), 2 Saba (D E half-flat F Gb A Bb C), 3 Hijaz (D Eb F# G A B half-flat C, coming down Bb), 4 Sikah (E half-flat F G A B half-flat C D), 5 Nahawand (C D Eb F G Ab B, coming down Bb), 6 Kurd (D Eb F G A Bb C), 7 Ajam (C D E F G A B). Written in quarter-tones: in 24 they are exact, in 31 within a few cents, in 12 and 19 approximate. The way down plays with melodic direction on

harp_parameter.name: maqam upper jins
harp_parameter.tooltip: swaps the maqam's upper jins for the one a player moves to, both ways: Rast to Suznak (Hijaz on G), Bayati to Husseini (B half-flat), Saba to Saba Zamzam, Hijaz to Hijazkar (C#), Sikah to Huzam, Nahawand to its Kurd form (Bb), Ajam to Nahawand on G (Bb); Kurd stays. Put it under the double tap to modulate as you play. 0 the maqam's own

harp_parameter.name: ribbon glide
harp_parameter.tooltip: how slowly the ribbon's pitch follows the finger, in milliseconds: longer smooths a jumpy reading and slurs fast moves, like portamento. 0 is the stock 10. On the stock strip, 60 to 120 turns its steps into a slide

harp_parameter.name: harp shuffling
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines different harp patterns. 0 is normal, 1 i with second, 2 is with fourth, 3 with sixth, 4 octaves, 5 chromatics and 6 useful when using a keymaster touchplate in Barry Harris mode

harp_parameter.name: octave change
harp_parameter.tooltip: changes the octave of the harp section up or down

harp_parameter.name: change held strings
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines whether a held harp note will change when changing chord

harp_parameter.name: amplitude
harp_parameter.tooltip: amplitude of the 12 initial oscillators

harp_parameter.name: string model
harp_parameter.tooltip: crossfades each harp string from its oscillator to a plucked string model, in percent. 0 is the oscillator alone, as before; 100 is the model alone: a burst of noise ringing round a loop the length of the string's period, which mellows as it dies away the way a real string does. Its pluck is brighter the harder the string is plucked (with touch velocity on), and it follows the ribbon's glide, the vibrato and the tuning. The envelope, filter and transient still shape it; an envelope with a quick attack and long decay lets the string ring as it would. A sampled harp voice (harp voice 1-5) plays instead of both, the model resting

harp_parameter.name: harp voice
harp_parameter.tooltip: (5: the song, a second of what plays into the minichord over USB, grabbed with phone deck) what each harp string sounds: 0 its own synth (the oscillator and string model), as before; 1 piano; 2 pizzicato strings; 3 choir; 4 a string quartet (cello low, viola in the middle, violin high). A sample runs through the string's envelope, filter and level, so the preset still shapes it, and follows the ribbon and the tuning. Samples rendered by the midi-js-soundfonts project: the piano from FluidR3 (CC BY 3.0), the others from Musyng Kite (CC BY-SA 3.0); see lib/minichord_samples

harp_parameter.name: string decay
harp_parameter.tooltip: how long the plucked string model rings, in seconds for it to die away by 60 dB, at any pitch. Short is a muted, nylon or koto-like pluck; long a ringing steel string or a harp left to sound

harp_parameter.name: string damping
harp_parameter.tooltip: how much faster the plucked string model's highs die away than its lows: 0 keeps it bright and metallic as it rings, high mellows it quickly to a round, soft tone, like gut or nylon

harp_parameter.name: waveform
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines the waveform amongst 12 oscillators. In order: sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, bandlimited pulse, pulse, reverse sawtooth, sample and hold, variable triangle, bandlimited sawtooth, reverse bandlimited sawtooth, bandlimited square.

harp_parameter.name: attack
harp_parameter.tooltip: attack time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: hold
harp_parameter.tooltip: hold time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: decay
harp_parameter.tooltip: decay time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: sustain
harp_parameter.tooltip: sustain level of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: release
harp_parameter.tooltip: release time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: retrigger release
harp_parameter.tooltip: retrigger time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: palm mute
harp_parameter.tooltip: lay a hand flat across the harp to stop every string ringing, the way a guitarist mutes with the palm: this many pads held at once reads as a palm rather than a strum. Pads under the palm stay silent until they are lifted, so the hand landing makes only a short muted chuck, but any other pad still plays: hold the mute with a few fingers and strum the rest. Another mute needs the palm lifted first. With pluck on lift, fingers placed on strings are a chord waiting to be played, so only pads that land together count, and a palm should be bigger than any chord you place: 6 or more A fingertip strum holds two or three pads at most, so 4 or 5 is a good start. At 0 there is no palm mute, as before

harp_parameter.name: palm mute release
harp_parameter.tooltip: how fast a palm mute stops the strings, in milliseconds: a few for a dead stop, longer for a softer damp. With harp pluck on lift, a finger on a ringing string stops it this fast too

harp_parameter.name: pluck on lift
harp_parameter.tooltip: when a harp string sounds. At 1 it sounds as the finger leaves the pad, the way a harp string does: touching a ringing string stops it, with the palm mute release, and nothing sounds while a pad is held. Strings can be placed ahead of time and lifted together for a chord or one by one for a roll, and since the note is chosen at the lift, placed under one chord and lifted under the next. A strum comes out a little later, by as long as the finger rests on each pad. At 0 it sounds as the finger touches the pad, as before

harp_parameter.name: koto press
harp_parameter.tooltip: with pluck on lift, a finger on a ringing string presses it instead of stopping it, the way a koto player presses a string beside the bridge, and the string bends up as far as it is pressed: this many semitones at a full press, 2 for a whole tone. Rest lightly, then press: easing off lets the pitch back down. Lifting a finger that pressed lets the string ring on at its own pitch; one that only rested on it plucks it again. Pluck with one hand and press with the other, or pluck a chord and bend one note of it. A ringing string is then stopped by a palm mute rather than a finger. On the stock strip and plates of twelve zones, not the ribbon or zipper 24. In MPE the bend goes out as the string's pitch bend. 0 is off: a finger stops a ringing string, as before

harp_parameter.name: koto press steps
harp_parameter.tooltip: counts koto press in steps of the tuning rather than semitones, so in 24 a koto press of 1 bends a quarter-tone and in 31 a diesis, the notes between the semitones a bend in semitones passes over. In twelve they are the same. 0 semitones, as before

harp_parameter.name: koto press snap
harp_parameter.tooltip: holds a koto press bend on each step it passes (each semitone, or each step of the tuning with koto press steps): this much of each step's width, in percent, plays the step in tune, and between them the pitch slides the rest of the way, as ribbon snap holds the ribbon to its strings. A press then lands on the shrutis rather than past them, and still never jumps. 0 smooth, as before; 100 steps from one to the next

harp_parameter.name: hammer-on
harp_parameter.tooltip: plucking on touch, a finger landing on the pad beside a string still held down takes that string over: it moves to the new note without being plucked again, the way a guitarist hammers onto the next fret, and slides on from pad to pad as the finger moves along the strip. Hold a string and tap the next one for a hammer-on or a trill: lifting the tapping finger pulls off back to the held note, and lifting the last finger lets the string ring out. Only a string that has rung for a moment (hammer-on time, 180 ms unless set) is taken over, so a strum still plucks every string, but a string held beside where you start a strum is moved rather than another plucked. Over midi the new note starts just before the old one ends, so a synth set to legato slides or hammers too. On the stock strip and plates of twelve zones, not with pluck on lift, the ribbon or zipper 24. 0 is off: every pad plucks its own string, as before

harp_parameter.name: hammer-on time
harp_parameter.tooltip: how long a string has to ring, in ms, before a finger landing beside it takes it over with hammer-on. 180, the usual, is longer than a slow strum's 150 ms from string to string, so a strum still plucks every string. Shorter, a grace note or a trill can follow its string at once: a piper's cuts and an oud's trills want 40 to 60 ms. Then a slow strum across a string still held moves that string instead of plucking the next, so strum quickly or lift first

harp_parameter.name: touch velocity
harp_parameter.tooltip: how much a light touch plays softer and darker than a firm one: the harder a string is plucked, the louder and brighter it sounds and the higher its midi velocity. 0 plays every pluck the same, as before. At 100 a really light touch is quiet and dark (24 dB down, two octaves of the string filter, a tenth of the velocity), while an ordinary strum plays nearly full, about 5 dB down. Read from how firmly the finger lands: a quick tap or strum reads firm, a slow one rolling onto each string softer. Plucking on lift, from how firmly the string was held. Also the depth of touch pressure

harp_parameter.name: touch pressure
harp_parameter.tooltip: a held string follows how hard it is pressed, so the fingers shape the note while they hold it. 0: off. 1: follow: pressing harder than it was plucked swells it louder and brighter, as far as touch velocity reaches, and easing off lets it back down. A finger usually eases off as it lifts, so a note pressed up can fade a little before it rings out. 2: swell only: pressing harder swells it and it keeps the firmest it has been until it is let go, so it always rings out from there. Either way its pressure goes out over midi as it is, as each voice's channel pressure in MPE and as polyphonic aftertouch otherwise. Plucking on lift, held strings are silent, so it only sends on the ribbon

harp_parameter.name: strum velocity
harp_parameter.tooltip: how much a slow strum plays softer and darker than a fast one: the faster a strum sweeps across the strings, the louder and brighter they sound and the higher their midi velocity. 0 is off. With touch velocity on as well, each string plays as firmly as the firmer of the two says. A strum is neighbouring strings plucked one after another the same way; the first string of each has nothing to measure, so it plays by touch (full if touch velocity is off). On the stock and zipper plates, not the ribbon

chord_parameter.name: chord shuffling
chord_parameter.tooltip: defines different chord patterns. 0 is normal, 1 to 4 is one octave up with different additional notes, 5 is two octave up

chord_parameter.name: octave change
chord_parameter.tooltip: changes the octave of the chord section up or down

chord_parameter.name: glide chords
chord_parameter.tooltip: changes the glide lenght between chords

chord_parameter.name: fingered glide
chord_parameter.tooltip: the chords glide only when the fingers move to the next chord while still holding the last, as a monosynth's fingered portamento does: roll from one chord onto the next for a slide, lift first and press for a clean change. Sharpening a held chord with the modifier, adding or letting go of a slash chord's bass, or changing a column's kind with a second button glide too, since a finger stays down through them. With hold on, the chord ringing after the fingers lift doesn't count: the next press starts on its pitch. Glide chords sets how long the glide is. Not in rhythm mode, which glides as glide chords says. 0: every change glides, as before

chord_parameter.name: chord inversion
chord_parameter.tooltip: voicing of the chord buttons. 0 is root position, 1 and 2 are the first and second inversions, 3 is the third inversion for seventh and sixth chords or the root position an octave up for triads

chord_parameter.name: press again in hold
chord_parameter.tooltip: with hold on, what pressing the chord that is ringing again does. 0: strikes it again (with retrigger on), as before. 1: climbs it an inversion each press, up to root position an octave higher, then back to where it began. 2: climbs that far and comes back down an inversion at a time. 3: an octave up, and back down on the next press. The climb starts from chord inversion and starts over with any other chord; with voice leading on, the climbed voicing is kept as played and the next chord is led from it. It strikes as it moves when retrigger is on, and slides the voices there when it is off. Only a fresh press counts, not rolling onto the chord from another

chord_parameter.name: chord spacing
chord_parameter.tooltip: how far apart the chord voices sit. 0=close (adjacent tones), 1=drop 2, 2=drop 3, 3=drop 2 and 4 (the most evenly spread), 4=spread the outer voices. Drops move a voice down an octave; a move that would leave the usable range is not made

chord_parameter.name: voice leading
chord_parameter.tooltip: place the chord voices to move as little as possible from the chord already sounding, the way a choir does, instead of building every chord upward from its root. 1 is on; 2 is strict, which also avoids parallel fifths and octaves, and the outer voices leaping into a fifth or octave, at the cost of a little more movement. Overrides the inversion setting while it is on. A slash chord keeps its bass on the note it names, in the octave nearest the chord already sounding, and the voices above it are led

chord_parameter.name: voice leading range
chord_parameter.tooltip: how far, in semitones, a voice led chord may sit outside where root position would have put it, converted to steps of the live division so it means the same interval in 12, 19 and 31. Small keeps the chords anchored where the buttons say, large lets them follow the previous chord further. Only used when voice leading is on

chord_parameter.name: slash level
chord_parameter.tooltip: level of the scale which will be affected when using slash chords

chord_parameter.name: slash voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: which of the four chord voices a slash replaces, counted from the bottom: 1 bass, 2 tenor, 3 alto, 4 soprano. At 0 slash level decides, as before. Bass is a slash chord in the usual sense, with the whole chord above it; the others change only that voice, for a melody note on top or a suspension inside the chord

chord_parameter.name: slash re-voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: with slash voice set to tenor, alto or soprano, the other three voices move to keep the chord whole around the slash note, as little as they can, instead of holding still. The bass always keeps the chord whole

chord_parameter.name: cantus
chord_parameter.tooltip: which chord voice the harp sets, the way slash voice lets a slash set one: 1 bass, 2 tenor, 3 alto, 4 soprano counted from the bottom, 5 whichever voice is nearest the note. The first string of each new harp gesture gives that voice its note (the rest of a strum does not). A chord tone keeps the chord whole around it; any other note is a passing tone that voice sings alone. It holds through a chord change when the new chord has the note, and lets go otherwise. A slash keeps any voice it holds. At 0 the harp leaves the chord alone, as before

chord_parameter.name: chord voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: (5: the song, a second of what plays into the minichord over USB, grabbed with phone deck) what each chord voice sounds: 0 its own oscillators, as before; 1 piano; 2 pizzicato strings; 3 choir; 4 a string quartet. A sample runs through the voice's envelope and filter, so the preset still shapes it. Samples rendered by the midi-js-soundfonts project: the piano from FluidR3 (CC BY 3.0), the others from Musyng Kite (CC BY-SA 3.0); see lib/minichord_samples

Counted as the note levels (first note to fourth note) are: the first is the bass and the fourth the top with the chords voiced as they come, with inversions and with voice leading; chord spacing without voice leading can reorder them. Each note has its own sample player, so this costs nothing more

chord_parameter.name: rhythm style
chord_parameter.tooltip: what rhythm mode plays. 0: the rythm pattern steps below, as it always has. The rest are written parts that follow whatever chord is held: 1 Alberti bass (lowest, top, middle, top in sixteenths), 2 waltz (oom-pah-pah, the bass alternating root and fifth), 3 boom-chick (root, chord, fifth, chord), 4 walking bass (root, third, fifth and a step into the next chord, under a Charleston comp), 5 boogie (root under a fifth rocking to the sixth), 6 Travis picking, 7 strummed guitar (down, down-up, up-down-up), 8 bossa nova, 9 arpeggio up, 10 arpeggio up and down, 11 ballad (bass held under chords pulsing in eighths), 12 reggae (chords on the offbeats), 13 6/8 arpeggio, 14 habanera. The first chord note is the bass part and the other three the chord part, each with its own note voice. Shuffle value swings them; voice leading makes the Alberti and the arpeggios move as a hand does

chord_parameter.name: rhythm bass
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the first chord note does under a rhythm style: 0 plays the style's bass part, 1 holds the chord's bass note as it does outside rhythm mode, 2 rests. Not for rhythm style 0

chord_parameter.name: rhythm chords
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the other three chord notes do under a rhythm style: 0 play the style's chord part, 1 hold the chord as outside rhythm mode (a bass line walking under a sustained pad), 2 rest (the bass line alone). Not for rhythm style 0

chord_parameter.name: rhythm follows hands
chord_parameter.tooltip: whether rhythm mode plays only while a chord is held. 0: it plays on, as it always has. 1: it sounds while a chord button is down and stops when you let go, the beat running on underneath so it comes back in time. 2: the same, and a chord pressed from silence starts the bar, as an Omnichord's sync start (not while following a MIDI clock)

chord_parameter.name: rhythm chord change
chord_parameter.tooltip: when a new chord comes into a rhythm style. 0: on its next note, and a chord pressed just after a beat (up to a quarter of a beat, 100 ms at most) still takes that beat. 1: on the next beat. 2: on the next bar, and a walking bass then steps into the chord waiting to come in. Rhythm style 0 keeps measure update

chord_parameter.name: rhythm articulation
chord_parameter.tooltip: how long a rhythm style's notes are held, in percent of their written length: lower is more staccato, higher more legato. Notes written to ring (the strummed guitar) ring until struck again whatever this is. Not for rhythm style 0, which has note pushed duration

chord_parameter.name: rhythm accents
chord_parameter.tooltip: how much a rhythm style's strong beats stand out from its weak ones, in percent of the written accents: 0 plays every note equally loud. Applies to the sound and to the midi velocity. Not for rhythm style 0

chord_parameter.name: tap tempo counts
chord_parameter.tooltip: what a tap on the hold button counts in rhythm mode. 0: a tap a beat, as before. 1: a tap an eighth, two to the beat, for tapping along with the pulse the pattern moves in. Either way the second tap sets the tempo, the next few refine it, and each tap puts the beat (or the eighth) where it fell

chord_parameter.name: MIDI chords
chord_parameter.tooltip: lets a computer, a keyboard or a sequencer choose rhythm mode's chords. 1: in rhythm mode, notes sent in on the chords' port and channel (MIDI port and chord channel) play the accompaniment rather than sounding themselves: what is held is read as a chord, its root and kind and the bass under it, and the rhythm style plays it in the voicing it came in. A note held, or the sustain pedal, counts as a hand on the chord buttons for rhythm follows hands; held chord voices sound it. The harp still follows the buttons. 0: notes sent in do as MIDI in plays says. Don't send the minichord's own chord notes back to it

chord_parameter.name: rhythm style B
chord_parameter.tooltip: a second style for the same song, the way an arranger keyboard has a main A and B: each fill plays into the next bar line and then switches from rhythm style to this one, or back. A verse in Travis picking and a chorus strummed, a walking bass and then a boogie. It starts from its own first bar where it comes in. It must count the bar the way rhythm style does (four with four, three with three); one in another metre is never switched to, and the fills only fill. 0: no B, fills only fill

chord_parameter.name: rhythm fill
chord_parameter.tooltip: plays a fill, a break or the ending in rhythm mode: writing it does one thing and it goes back to 0, never kept in a preset. 1 a fill: the style's own fill bar from now to the next bar line (or the one after, if less than a beat is left), each style's in its own idiom and leading the bass into the chord there, then the other style if rhythm style B is set. 2 a break: every part rests up to the bar line and comes back on the downbeat. 3 the ending: a fill, then the chord struck on the bar line and left ringing, and rhythm mode goes off. Assign the double tap to it (double tap control 315) for a fill each double tap, or a break or the ending with double tap value 2 or 3. Control changes 109, 110 and 111 do the same on any channel

chord_parameter.name: fill on modifier and hold
chord_parameter.tooltip: in rhythm mode, holding the modifier and tapping hold plays a fill (see rhythm fill) instead of tapping the tempo, so a fill is there without giving up a double tap. With a chord held the modifier sharpens it, as always, so it is for a chord left playing. 0: hold taps the tempo whatever the modifier does, as before

chord_parameter.name: rhythm intro
chord_parameter.tooltip: rhythm mode starts with a bar of the style's fill, a pickup into the groove, before the pattern begins. With rhythm follows hands at 2 it plays from the press. 0: the pattern from the first beat, as before

chord_parameter.name: rhythm ending
chord_parameter.tooltip: the long press on hold that turns rhythm mode off plays an ending first: the style's fill up to the next bar line, then the chord struck there and left ringing as rhythm mode goes off (hold the chord to keep it sounding). A second long press during the ending stops at once. 0: the long press stops it there and then, as before

chord_parameter.name: rhythm palm break
chord_parameter.tooltip: in rhythm mode a palm mute on the harp stops the accompaniment too, the band's stop: every part rests up to the next bar line (or the one after, if less than a beat is left) and comes back on the downbeat. Needs palm mute on. 0: the palm stops only the strings, as before

chord_parameter.name: drums
chord_parameter.tooltip: rhythm mode plays drums with the accompaniment: a synthesized kit, a groove that follows the rhythm's tempo, tap, MIDI clock and the phone's beat, its own fills in the fills, silent in a break, a crash where a fill lands and on the ending's last chord. Without a groove chosen, each rhythm style plays its own drum part: a waltz waltz drums, the walking bass a swing ride, the bossa nova a bossa. 0 no drums, as before

chord_parameter.name: drum groove
chord_parameter.tooltip: the drums' groove instead of the rhythm style's own part: 1 rock, 2 pop eighths, 3 pop sixteenths, 4 ballad, 5 funk, 6 disco, 7 motown, 8 shuffle, 9 jazz swing, 10 waltz, 11 march, 12 second line, 13 country two-beat, 14 folk, 15 six eight, 16 habanera, 17 house, 18 trap, 19 amen-style break, 20 funky drummer-style, 21 think-style break, 22 boom bap, 23 drum and bass, 24 lo-fi, 25 son clave, 26 rumba clave, 27 bossa nova, 28 samba, 29 cumbia, 30 baiao, 31 salsa, 32 one drop, 33 dembow, 34 soca, 35 afrobeat, 36 12/8 bell, 37 highlife, 38 maqsum, 39 baladi, 40 saidi, 41 kehrwa, 42 dadra, 43 teental. Played in our own synthesized sounds; the famous breaks re-played, not sampled. One in another metre than the style keeps its own length. 0 the rhythm style's own drum part

chord_parameter.name: drum groove B
chord_parameter.tooltip: the groove after a fill switches to rhythm style B: 0 as before the switch (the groove chosen, or style B's own drum part if none is), else one of drum groove's list

chord_parameter.name: drum kit
chord_parameter.tooltip: the kit the drums play: 1 808, 2 909, 3 CR-78, 4 studio, 5 brushes, 6 boom bap, 7 world percussion, 8 tabla and doumbek, 9 trap, 10 house, 11 glitch. Each groove has its own kit (the breaks the dusty boom bap kit, the son clave the world percussion, maqsum and teental the tabla and doumbek); this plays any groove on another. The trap kit's kick is an 808 bass on the chord's root. 0 the groove's own

chord_parameter.name: drum level
chord_parameter.tooltip: how loud the drums are, beside the chords and the harp

chord_parameter.name: drum humanize
chord_parameter.tooltip: how loosely the drums play: each hit up to 15 ms late and 20% softer at 100, at random, as a drummer pushes and lays back. 0 dead on the grid

chord_parameter.name: drum MIDI out
chord_parameter.tooltip: each drum hit, and each pad on the harp in harp drums, goes out on MIDI channel 10 in General MIDI's drum map (kick 36, snare 38, side stick 37, clap 39, hats 42 and 46, crash 49, toms 45 and 50, congas 64 and 63, cowbell 56, maracas 70), so a computer records the drums or plays them on its own kit: 1 on port 1, 2 on port 2. 0 off

chord_parameter.name: count-in
chord_parameter.tooltip: rhythm mode starts with a bar of sticks, a click on each beat and the first louder, before the intro or the groove, so a band can come in together. A MIDI clock's Start, or the bar starting on a press, counts itself. 0 straight in

chord_parameter.name: drums only
chord_parameter.tooltip: with drums on, the accompaniment rests and the drums play alone, for playing the chords and the harp over a beat; fills, breaks and the ending as before. 0 both

chord_parameter.name: harp drums
chord_parameter.tooltip: the harp's twelve strings play the drum kit instead of notes, the lowest string the kick: kick, snare, side stick, clap, closed hat, open hat, cymbal, low tom, high tom, low conga, high conga, bell. As hard as they are struck, with or without rhythm mode, and out over MIDI with drum MIDI out. The kit is drum kit's, or the groove's. While on, the harp ribbon, the zipper plate, hammer-on and palm mute rest. 0 the strings play notes, as before

chord_parameter.name: tabla laya
chord_parameter.tooltip: how fast the tabla's thekas (kehrwa, dadra, teental) go against the tempo. As written, 0, each bol is a step: teental's sixteen to a beat's four steps, so a medium teental needs the tempo near 30 and a slow (vilambit) one is slower than it goes. 1 a bol a beat: the tempo counts matras, as a tabla player counts them, and teental's cycle is sixteen beats, four bars, kehrwa's eight, dadra's six (two bars of three); 2 two bols a beat (dugun); 3 four (chaugun). Stretched, a fill plays the theka on to its half and then the tihai as written, and the theka starts again on sam where the tihai lands. The other grooves keep their time

chord_parameter.name: drum reverb
chord_parameter.tooltip: how much of the drums goes into the reverb, in percent, harp drums too; the drums stay as loud dry. The reverb is the one the harp and the chords share, its room set by reverb size and the rest. 0 dry, as before
